drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) combined with a Thiazide Diuretic
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines in one pill to make it easier to control your blood pressure. Keeping blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from serious problems.
how_it_works: Telmisartan works by blocking a chemical in your body that tightens your blood vessels, allowing them to relax and open up so blood can flow more easily. Hydrochlorothiazide is a mild water pill that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and fluid from your body, which also lowers blood pressure. Together, these two medicines work as a team to bring your blood pressure down more effectively than either one alone.
common_side_effects: Dizziness especially when standing up quickly, headache, feeling tired, increased urination (from the water pill), low potassium levels which may cause muscle cramps or weakness, and mild stomach upset. Most side effects are mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, liver disease, diabetes, or low potassium levels. This medicine can cause dizziness so be careful driving or standing up quickly. Avoid taking with potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you to. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Common strengths include 40mg/12.5mg or 80mg/12.5mg or 80mg/25mg. Your doctor will choose the right strength for you. Try to take it at the same time every day and never skip doses, even if you feel fine.
